versions.prompt: An original, extremely subtle instrumental underscore for a cinematic historical video game scene set inside John Harrison's clockmaker workshop in London, England, in 1760. Evoking the intellectual spirit of eighteenth-century Britain, scientific curiosity, mechanical invention, craftsmanship, patience and the quiet pursuit of precision. Inspired by late Baroque and early Classical chamber music heard in eighteenth-century Britain; do not imitate any existing composition. Calm, serene, intimate, dignified and contemplative. Use very soft cello, sustained viola, delicate violin harmonies and occasional sparse harpsichord notes. Slow tempo, approximately 55–60 BPM. The arrangement must remain minimal, spacious and unobtrusive, almost like a gentle musical presence in the background. An elderly male narrator will speak over this music. Leave ample acoustic and emotional space for his voice. Convey subtle warmth, quiet ingenuity and the atmosphere of an inventor's workshop. Use sparse musical phrases, restrained harmonic movement and soft sustained textures, allowing moments of near silence. Avoid prominent melodies, busy harpsichord passages, virtuosic runs, rhythmic complexity, dramatic crescendos or strong musical accents. No vocals, no lyrics, no narration, no percussion, no modern electronic instruments, no clock ticking, no mechanical sound effects and no environmental noises. The music should remain gentle and emotionally restrained throughout, with a subtle sense of mystery and anticipation. Create a complete instrumental underscore of approximately two minutes and forty-five seconds.
